title: A land that stops after it removed the worker's worktree prints the command that brings the worktree back for the fix
goal: When backlog.py land stops at a step after it released the worker's worktree (lint, eval, stale, the push), its stop message names the git worktree add command that checks work/<id> out again at the same path, so the orchestrator fixes the branch without finding the path by hand; at SP-up5wchen the land of ST-4ehra2pk stopped at lint twice and the orchestrator re-added the removed worktree each time.

run: import sys;t=open('_tools/bl_land.py',encoding='utf-8').read();sys.exit(0 if 'worktree add' in t else 1)

notes: Merged from ST-iviphkbm “land keeps the worker's worktree until its push has succeeded (second-project run)” at the 2026-10-12 draft triage: land must release the worktree before it rebases (git rebase needs the branch free), and the branch keeps every commit after a failed push, so keeping the worktree is not workable. ST-ht2kk34y already covers a stop at lint, eval, stale or push by printing the git worktree add command. Absorb only a push-failure case into its land_e2e test. Its goal: land removes a finished worker's worktree only after the push step exits 0, so a failed push leaves the worktree to resume in Its checks: {"run": ["python3", "_tools/tests.py", "-k", "land_keeps_worktree_until_push"]}
